gloss: mekabu; the frilly root part of wakame seaweed

definitions.explanation: The thick, ruffled part at the base of a wakame frond, sold chopped and eaten for its slippery texture. Usually written in hiragana or katakana.

examples.japanese: めかぶは{体|からだ}にいいそうだ。
examples.english: They say mekabu is good for you.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ごはんに、めかぶと{納豆|なっとう}を{混|ま}ぜて{食|た}べるのが{習慣|しゅうかん}になっている。
examples.english: Mixing mekabu with natto for breakfast has become a habit of mine.

notes:
The base of a wakame plant, just above the holdfast. When chopped it becomes very slippery, and that texture is the point of the dish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {刻|きざ}みめかぶ: chopped mekabu (the usual supermarket form)
- めかぶ{納豆|なっとう}: mekabu mixed with natto
- めかぶの{酢|す}の{物|もの}: mekabu in vinegar dressing
- ねばねばする: to be sticky and slippery

SIMILAR WORDS:
- わかめ: wakame — the leafy blade of the same plant, sold separately
- もずく: mozuku — a different slippery seaweed, usually served in vinegar
